Density contour plot

Source: R/express.R
px_density_contour.Rd

In a density contour plot, rows of data_frame are grouped together into contour marks to visualize the 2D distribution of an aggregate function histfunc (e.g. the count or sum) of the value z.

Usage

px_density_contour(
  data_frame = NULL,
  x = NULL,
  y = NULL,
  z = NULL,
  color = NULL,
  facet_row = NULL,
  facet_col = NULL,
  facet_col_wrap = 0,
  facet_row_spacing = NULL,
  facet_col_spacing = NULL,
  hover_name = NULL,
  hover_data = NULL,
  animation_frame = NULL,
  animation_group = NULL,
  category_orders = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  orientation = NULL,
  color_discrete_sequence = NULL,
  color_discrete_map = NULL,
  marginal_x = NULL,
  marginal_y = NULL,
  trendline = NULL,
  trendline_options = NULL,
  trendline_color_override = NULL,
  trendline_scope = "trace",
  log_x = FALSE,
  log_y = FALSE,
  range_x = NULL,
  range_y = NULL,
  histfunc = NULL,
  histnorm = NULL,
  nbinsx = NULL,
  nbinsy = NULL,
  text_auto = FALSE,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  template = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL
)

Arguments

data_frame

A data.frame, data.table, list or matrix. Needed for column names to be used in the other arguments; if NULL, a data frame is built from the vectors given in the other arguments.

x

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to position marks along the x axis in cartesian coordinates.

y

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to position marks along the y axis in cartesian coordinates.

z

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to position marks along the z axis in cartesian coordinates.

color

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to assign color to marks.

facet_row

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to assign marks to facetted subplots in the vertical direction.

facet_col

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to assign marks to facetted subplots in the horizontal direction.

facet_col_wrap

Maximum number of facet columns. Wraps the column variable at this width, so that the column facets span multiple rows. Ignored if 0, and forced to 0 if facet_row or a marginal is set.

facet_row_spacing

Spacing between facet rows, in paper units. Default is 0.03 or 0.07 when facet_col_wrap is used.

facet_col_spacing

Spacing between facet columns, in paper units Default is 0.02.

hover_name

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector appear in bold in the hover tooltip.

hover_data

Extra data to show in the hover tooltip: column names (a character vector or a formula such as ~c(a, b)), or a named list with column names as names and values TRUE (default formatting), FALSE (hide the column, e.g. one shown by default), a d3-format string such as ":.3f", a vector of data, or a list of a format string or TRUE and a vector of data.

animation_frame

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to assign marks to animation frames.

animation_group

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to provide object-constancy across animation frames: rows with matching animation_groups will be treated as if they describe the same object in each frame.

category_orders

Named list mapping column names to the order of their values in axes, legends and facets, e.g. list(day = c("Thur", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")). By default values appear in the order first encountered, or in level order for factors.

labels

Named character vector or list mapping column names to the labels to use for axis titles, legend entries and hover text, e.g. c(gdpPercap = "GDP per capita").

orientation

(default "v" if x and y are provided and both continuous or both categorical, otherwise "v"("h") if x(y) is categorical and y(x) is continuous, otherwise "v"("h") if only x(y) is provided)

color_discrete_sequence

Character vector of colors, e.g. px_colors$qualitative$Set1. Values of color are assigned colors in order (cycling), unless set in color_discrete_map. Defaults to the template's colorway.

color_discrete_map

Named character vector or list mapping values of color to colors, overriding color_discrete_sequence. If the values of color are colors, px_identity() (or "identity") uses them directly.

marginal_x

One of "rug", "box", "violin", or "histogram". If set, a horizontal subplot is drawn above the main plot, visualizing the x-distribution.

marginal_y

One of "rug", "box", "violin", or "histogram". If set, a vertical subplot is drawn to the right of the main plot, visualizing the y-distribution.

trendline

One of "ols" (ordinary least squares regression), "lowess" (locally weighted smoothing), "rolling", "expanding" or "ewm" (exponentially weighted moving average). A trendline is drawn for each discrete color/symbol group; configure it with trendline_options. Fitted OLS models are available from px_get_trendline_results().

trendline_options

Named list of options for the trendline function: for "ols", add_constant, log_x and log_y; for "lowess", frac; for "rolling", window, min_periods, center and function ("mean", "median", "sum", "min", "max", "std", "var", "count"); for "expanding", min_periods and function; for "ewm", one of com, span, halflife or alpha, and adjust.

trendline_color_override

Valid CSS color. If provided, and if trendline is set, all trendlines will be drawn in this color rather than in the same color as the traces from which they draw their inputs.

trendline_scope

If "trace", then one trendline is drawn per trace (i.e. per color, symbol, facet, animation frame etc) and if "overall" then one trendline is computed for the entire dataset, and replicated across all facets.

log_x

If TRUE, the x-axis is log-scaled in cartesian coordinates.

log_y

If TRUE, the y-axis is log-scaled in cartesian coordinates.

range_x

If provided, overrides auto-scaling on the x-axis in cartesian coordinates.

range_y

If provided, overrides auto-scaling on the y-axis in cartesian coordinates.

histfunc

One of "count", "sum", "avg", "min", or "max". Function used to aggregate values for summarization (note: can be normalized with histnorm).

histnorm

One of "percent", "probability", "density", or "probability density" If NULL, the output of histfunc is used as is. If "probability", the output of histfunc for a given bin is divided by the sum of the output of histfunc for all bins. If "percent", the output of histfunc for a given bin is divided by the sum of the output of histfunc for all bins and multiplied by 100. If "density", the output of histfunc for a given bin is divided by the size of the bin. If "probability density", the output of histfunc for a given bin is normalized such that it corresponds to the probability that a random event whose distribution is described by the output of histfunc will fall into that bin.

nbinsx

Positive integer. Sets the number of bins along the x axis.

nbinsy

Positive integer. Sets the number of bins along the y axis.

text_auto

If TRUE or a string, the x or y or z values will be displayed as text, depending on the orientation A string like ".2f" will be interpreted as a texttemplate numeric formatting directive.

title

The figure title.

subtitle

The figure subtitle.

template

A template name (see template_names()) or a template list. Defaults to default_template().

width

The figure width in pixels.

height

The figure height in pixels.

Value

A go_figure().

See also

Other plotly express: px_area(), px_bar(), px_bar_polar(), px_box(), px_choropleth(), px_choropleth_map(), px_density_heatmap(), px_density_map(), px_ecdf(), px_funnel(), px_funnel_area(), px_histogram(), px_icicle(), px_imshow(), px_line(), px_line_3d(), px_line_geo(), px_line_map(), px_line_polar(), px_line_ternary(), px_parallel_categories(), px_parallel_coordinates(), px_pie(), px_scatter(), px_scatter_3d(), px_scatter_geo(), px_scatter_map(), px_scatter_matrix(), px_scatter_polar(), px_scatter_ternary(), px_strip(), px_sunburst(), px_timeline(), px_treemap(), px_violin()

Examples

px_data_tips() |> px_density_contour(x = ~total_bill, y = ~tip)
